message.subject: Spray nozzle blocked on new bottle (ORD-20113)
message.body:
Hello,

My new spray arrived on Monday (order ORD-20113) and the nozzle doesn't seem to work. I've pressed it maybe ten or fifteen times to prime it, the way I normally would with a new one, but nothing comes out, just a click. The cap was on properly and the box looked fine, so I don't think it was damaged in the post.

I haven't tried to take the top off or force it, as I wasn't sure whether that would make things worse. I still have a little left in the old bottle for today and tomorrow.

What would you like me to do?

Thanks,
Chidi Eze

policy.label: Policy P11.1: Product questions
policy.text:
Storage. Keep products below 25°C, out of direct sunlight, in their original packaging with the lid closed tightly, and out of reach of children and pets. They do not need to go in the fridge unless the label says so. Do not leave them in a car. Some oils can thicken or look cloudy when cold.

If a product looks, smells or tastes different, has been left somewhere hot, or a spray or dropper is not working, ask the patient not to use it until a pharmacist has checked. A pharmacist contacts them within 1 business day and arranges a replacement if needed. Agents never say a product is safe, fine or OK to use. If the patient asks whether it is still safe or OK to use, that is a clinical question: it goes to the clinician queue with no drafted reply (see clinical questions).

Packaging. Orders arrive in plain outer packaging. The label shows the patient's name and address only; it does not name the product or say it is medicine.

Availability and substitutions. If a product is out of stock, a clinician or pharmacist decides on any alternative, and the patient is told before anything changes. A different bottle size or format also needs a clinician's approval. Agents never recommend, compare or promote products. Unused or damaged medicine can be taken to any pharmacy for safe disposal.

policy.label: Policy P4.2: Late, lost, damaged or wrong orders
policy.text:
Late orders. 1 business day past the ETA: share the tracking and reassure the patient. 2 business days past the ETA: open a trace with Courierline, which takes up to 3 business days, and tell the patient we have done it. 5 business days past the ETA, or when Courierline confirms the parcel is lost: reship at no cost. Every reship of a prescription medicine needs pharmacist sign-off, usually the same business day, and is dispatched within 1 business day of sign-off.

Marked delivered but not received: ask the patient to check safe spots and with neighbours, and open a trace straight away. If the parcel is not found within 3 business days, reship at no cost.

Damaged or leaking: ask for a photo within 7 days of delivery and ask the patient not to use the damaged item. After pharmacist sign-off we reship at no cost. The damaged item does not need to come back; any pharmacy can dispose of it safely.

Wrong item: ask the patient not to use it. A pharmacist contacts them within 1 business day and the right item is reshipped at no cost.

Never promise a delivery date beyond the ETA shown on the order.

policy.label: Policy P2.1: Contact hours and response targets
policy.text:
Support hours, in local time. United Kingdom: Monday to Friday 9 am to 6 pm, UK time. The team is closed on national public holidays in each country, but the on-call clinician still covers urgent safety messages 24 hours a day.

Response targets. Live chat: first reply within 5 minutes during support hours. Email: first reply within 4 business hours. Messages that arrive out of hours are answered by 10 am the next business day. Clinical questions: a clinician replies within 1 business day, and within 4 business hours for side effects. Urgent safety messages: a clinician makes contact within 1 hour, at any time (see the urgent safety sections).
